clue.text: Unimpeded zone in county town, wherein food can be long stored (12, two words)

definitions.text: wherein food can be long stored

indicators.note: the first phrase is placed in the middle of the town's name, so 'in' asks for one inside the other

blocks.note: Chester is the county town of Cheshire
unimpeded means free
Z is an abbreviation for zone

explanation.surface: A cleared area inside a county town, where provisions are kept for the long haul.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wherein' does double duty: it ends the container signal and begins the definition, a place in which food is kept.
explanation.definitionFit: A chest freezer is a large lidded box-shaped freezer used for keeping food frozen over long periods.

clue.text: Bogy with base metal underneath

definitions.note: 'metal' is a verb here: to sheathe the underside with metal

blocks.note: bogy is slang for a policeman, as is copper
the base of something is its bottom

explanation.surface: A goblin set on a lower layer of cheap metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'base metal' reads as one phrase, but 'base' belongs to the wordplay and 'metal' is a verb in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To copper-bottom a ship is to sheathe its hull below the waterline with copper plating, i.e. to cover its underside in metal.

clue.text: Pester prince, roller in the grass?

indicators.note: the car is placed in the grass, so 'in' puts one piece inside the other

blocks.note: hay is dried grass
a Roller is slang for a Rolls-Royce, abbreviated RR

explanation.surface: Bothering a young royal who is rolling about on the lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: Two definitions plus a third route: a Roller is slang for a Rolls-Royce, and the question mark flags the car rather than a garden roller.
explanation.definitionFit: To harry is to harass persistently, and Prince Harry is a well-known royal of that name.

clue.text: Indolent skiver maybe appearing in court once

indicators.note: something appearing in a place is found inside it, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: to sue was an old word for to woo or court
a skiver is a variant of skewer, and a pin is a kind of skewer

explanation.surface: A lazy shirker turning up in a court of law in times past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skiver' suggests a shirker, which matches 'Indolent' nicely; here it is the dialect form of skewer.
explanation.definitionFit: Supine, literally lying face up, is used figuratively for passive, inactive or lazy.

clue.text: Maniple made of woollen fabric, length short inside

indicators.note: being short inside means lacking something in the middle, so a letter is removed from within the word

blocks.note: flannel is a soft woollen fabric
L is the abbreviation for length

explanation.surface: A church vestment woven from wool, a little short in the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: One of the two Ls of FLANNEL is lost from the inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A fannel (or fanon) is another name for the maniple, the strip of cloth worn on a priest's left arm.

clue.text: Takes part in rerun of Cresta misguidedly

indicators.note: something done misguidedly goes wrong, so the letters end up in a different order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone joins a repeat run of the Cresta toboggan course without good sense.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as RE-ACTS: acts again. The Cresta Run is a famous toboggan course in St Moritz.
explanation.definitionFit: To re-act is to act again, i.e. to perform a part once more in a repeat performance.

clue.text: Chemical compound finished holding them up

indicators.note: one word holding another has it inside, so the second goes into the first
in a down clue going up means reading from the bottom, so the result is read backwards

blocks.note: fully ripened or matured, finished
'em is the colloquial short form of them

explanation.surface: A finished chemical is holding them back from progress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'them' becomes the colloquial 'em, and in a down clue 'up' reverses the whole construction.
explanation.definitionFit: An epimer is one of a pair of isomeric compounds differing in configuration at only one asymmetric carbon atom.

clue.text: Big business in Japan or South Africa, one mad on uranium

indicators.note: one thing on another in a down clue is placed above it, so the pieces follow in sequence

blocks.note: ZA is the international vehicle code for South Africa
Roman numeral one
bats is slang for mad
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: Corporate giants in two countries, with one crazed figure keen on nuclear fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or South Africa' reads as an alternative country, but 'or' is only a link and South Africa is ZA.
explanation.definitionFit: The zaibatsu were the huge family-controlled industrial and financial conglomerates of Japan.

clue.text: Place of detention can render me unsettled, tense inside (12, two words)

indicators.note: unsettled letters are disturbed from their order and rearranged
the grammatical abbreviation goes inside the other letters

blocks.note: taken as written
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A prisoner complains that the place they are held makes them anxious and on edge.
explanation.walkthrough: T joins the eleven letters of 'can render me' and all twelve are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A remand centre is an institution where accused people are held in custody while awaiting trial.

clue.text: Small group of feathers, every one containing a dash of umber

indicators.note: containing means holding something within, so one piece goes inside another
a dash is a tiny amount, so only the opening letter of the word is taken

blocks.note: every one of them is all of them
a means one
the first letter of umber

explanation.surface: A tuft of plumage, each feather tipped with a touch of brown pigment.
explanation.walkthrough: U goes inside ALL, then A follows. Umber is a brown earth pigment.
explanation.definitionFit: The alula, or bastard wing, is the small cluster of feathers on a bird's thumb at the front of the wing.

clue.text: Rabble as of old support rising for example

indicators.note: in a down clue something rising reads from the bottom up, so it runs backwards

blocks.note: a leg is a support, as of a table
e.g. abbreviates for example

explanation.surface: An old-style mob, its support climbing, for instance.
explanation.definitionFit: Legge is an obsolete word for the common people or a rabble, hence the archaic flag in 'as of old'.

clue.text: Flood bringing core of slurry to the fore?

indicators.note: the middle letter is taken out of its place and moved, so it is removed from the centre first
to the fore means at the front, so the moved letter is placed first in the sequence

blocks.note: a paste is a thick slurry

explanation.surface: A flood that sweeps the thick sludge up to the front.
explanation.walkthrough: The centre letter of PASTE, its S, is moved to the front, as 'to the fore' says.
explanation.definitionFit: A spate is a sudden flood or freshet in a river, especially after heavy rain.

clue.text: Coup, leaderless, yet solvent

indicators.note: without a leader means the word loses its head, so its opening letter goes

blocks.note: a strike is a sudden success, a coup

explanation.surface: A coup without its ringleader that still leaves the country solvent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solvent' looks like financial health; it is the chemical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Trike is the short name for trichloroethylene, a widely used industrial solvent and degreaser.

clue.text: Pungent alcohol derivative for getting plane in motion

indicators.note: something in motion is moving about, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: pro means in favour of, for
taken as written

explanation.surface: A strong-smelling spirit-based fuel is in favour of getting an aircraft moving.
explanation.definitionFit: Propenal, or acrolein, is a sharp-smelling aldehyde made by dehydrating glycerol, an alcohol.

clue.text: Old-fashioned groom, puritan about love, note

indicators.note: about means around, so one word encloses the other

blocks.note: a prig is a self-righteous, puritanical person
love is zero in tennis, O
N is short for note

explanation.surface: An old-school bridegroom, a strait-laced type in love, makes a note.
explanation.walkthrough: O goes inside PRIG, then N follows. 'Groom' suggests a bridegroom, but here it is the verb: to trim or tidy.
explanation.definitionFit: Proign is an obsolete form of prune, in the sense of preening or grooming oneself.

clue.text: What'll determine root growth in agronomic ambiance

indicators.note: in means the letters lie within the following phrase, running across its two words

blocks.note: spans the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: An agricultural setting decides how well a plant's roots develop.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural is apt because 'What'll' covers more than one.
explanation.definitionFit: Cambia are the layers of dividing tissue in roots and stems that produce new growth in thickness.

clue.text: In emergency, stop multiplication of parts

indicators.note: the second word is placed in the first, so one sits inside the other

blocks.note: an emergency is a crisis
ho is an old call to stop or halt

explanation.surface: In an emergency, call a halt to things multiplying.
explanation.walkthrough: HO for 'stop' is an old interjection calling a halt, also used as a noun for a stop or limit.
explanation.definitionFit: In botany chorisis is the splitting of a floral organ into several, so the parts are multiplied.

clue.text: Bit of fine tuning, unconvincing after time

indicators.note: one thing coming after another places it second, setting the order of the pieces

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
an unconvincing argument is weak

explanation.surface: A small adjustment that, given time, still fails to persuade.
explanation.definitionFit: A tweak is a small adjustment made to improve something, a piece of fine tuning.

clue.text: Service (as in some bars) male getting into dance?

indicators.note: getting into something means going inside it, so one piece is placed within the other

blocks.note: a reel is a lively Scottish dance
he is the male pronoun

explanation.surface: Service at a bar, with a man joining a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bars' suggests pubs, but these are heel bars, kiosks that repair shoes while you wait.
explanation.definitionFit: To reheel shoes is to fit them with new heels, the routine repair job done at a heel bar.

clue.text: Strode out in good order maybe

indicators.note: out suggests disorder or being put out of place, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone marched out in a tidy, disciplined fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' flags that the definition is one sense among several of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that are sorted have been arranged properly, put in good order.

clue.text: What's brewing in Scotland? Run in home of old runners!

indicators.note: one letter is placed in the other phrase, so it sits inside

blocks.note: Bow Street (Bow St) was the base of the Bow Street Runners, London's early police
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: A Scottish brew, with a nod to a run in the home of the old police force.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bow Street Runners were London's first professional police, based in Bow Street.
explanation.definitionFit: Browst is a Scots word for a brewing, the quantity brewed at one time.

clue.text: What gets back up, having to accept recipe less well cooked

indicators.note: going up in a down clue reads the letters from the bottom, so backwards

blocks.note: the rear is the back part of anything
R (from Latin recipe, take) heads a prescription

explanation.surface: Something that rises again after taking in a recipe for meat that is less done.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes into the reversed back word. Recipe as R is the old prescription sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Rare meat is lightly cooked, so rarer meat has been cooked less thoroughly.

clue.text: Wife's sweet cake brought up form of decay (6, two words)

indicators.note: in a down clue bringing something up reads it bottom to top, so in reverse

blocks.note: a torte is a rich sweet cake

explanation.walkthrough: The cake comes with the wife after it, and the whole lot is read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Wet rot is fungal decay of timber that is kept damp.

clue.text: Thoroughly soak mesh climbing frame for drying

clue.text: Sweet wine estaminet preferred to dry one mostly

explanation.definitionFit: Barsac is a sweet white dessert wine from the Bordeaux region, near Sauternes.

clue.text: Bits of Bach, ludicrous on war trumpets

blocks.note: the initials of the two words

explanation.walkthrough: 'trumpets' looks like a noun for the instruments; it is the verb.

clue.text: Manchu minister, a chess piece capturing bishop

clue.text: Ranger, me, captivated by crowd noise?

blocks.note: the roar of the crowd
taken as written

clue.text: Ridge, part one's cut off in etc, coming from behind

clue.text: Melanesian canoe, character amidships making way for number

the middle letter of the canoe word

Roman numeral one
